messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a spike of 413s from the embeddings route in staging when clients send mixed-dim batches. Can we align on a short-term policy?
anya: ugh yep saw it too. It's mostly when the client packs 1536 and 384 vectors together. splitter currently rejects if total bytes > 8MB.
li: the 8MB rule was a blunt instrument. we need to either: (A) fail fast with a clear error + hint, or (B) auto-split and route, but that has quota/accounting implications.
mike: Agree. For (B) we need a consistent accounting model so customers don't get surprised on billing and console charts.
anya: proposal: include X-Embed-Dims and X-Embed-Chunk-Count headers in the request/response so console can show pre-split vs post-split unit usage.
jordan: header idea is fine. also add telemetry event names: embed.preflight, embed.splitter.invoked, embed.splitter.fallback. That helps correlate 413 spikes.
sam: sample preflight response we could return for fastfail: 
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"batch_oversize","max_bytes":8388608,"hint":"send smaller batches or enable chunking via ?split_hint=true","preflight":{"dims":[1536,384,384],"estimated_bytes":9231100}}
```
mike: love the hint field. Console UX should map that to an action button: "Split request (best-effort)" and call the same API with chunking param.
li: runtime note: auto-splitting at ingress is doable but we need to ensure correctness for affinity routing — if a tenant pins a model variant that only supports fixed-dim packing, we must preserve that routing.
anya: related quota question: do we charge split requests as one original request or as N subrequests? What do we want customers to see?
jordan: I'd prefer charging based on tokens/bytes actually served (post-split). That matches infra costs, but need to communicate transparently in billing and route dashboards.
sam: ops concern: if post-split billing is used, a malicious client could craft many small dims to game unit pricing. we need a softcap + anomaly alerting.
mike: console changes: new dashboard panel "Embed split rate" (percent of batches that were split) and "Avg post-split bytes per original request". Those tie to billing deltas.
li: telemetry schema draft: 
```
embed.preflight => {tenant_id, request_id, dims:[], bytes_est, preflight_result: PASS|SPLIT|REJECT}
embed.splitter => {request_id, chunks: N, chunk_sizes:[], route_targets:[]}
embed.billing_hint => {request_id, estimated_units_before, estimated_units_after}
```
anya: one more UX thought: for client SDKs, return a structured error with a recommended automatic retry strategy. e.g., {type: 'split', chunk_hint: 512, retry_after: 0}.
jordan: rollout plan: feature-flag splitter.v2 to 10% tenants, monitor split-rate, billing-delta, and 413 count. add canary flag to route certain tenants to a "split-aware" runtime lane.
sam: approved. add canary tag in infra: tag=embed-split-canary. deploy-bot: deploy request queued for canary size 10%
deploy-bot: @sam deployment started for tag=embed-split-canary on eng-platform-staging at 1768501220 :rocket:
li: follow-ups: (1) implement headers + telemetry; (2) console wireframe for split action; (3) billing decision doc; (4) rate-limiter adjustments to avoid split storms.
mike: I'll take the console wireframe.
anya: I'll own SDK error shape + client retry guidance.
sam: li + I will handle runtime changes + preflight API. I'll open RFC with timeline.
jordan: Add a dashboard alert: if embed.splitter.invoked_rate > 5% AND billing_delta > 10% in 1h, auto-revert canary.
sam: sounds good. thanks all :thumbsup:
